message.content:
In the codebase at /bench/home/work, find which single function or method declared under internal/ has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in), and roughly how many callers it has.

Strategy:
1. First, list files under internal/ to understand the package structure.
2. Look at key files like internal/util/util.go, internal/base/resource_name.go, internal/filter/ functions, internal/markdown/markdown.go to find exported functions.
3. For each candidate exported function, use grep to count how many times it's called across the entire codebase (excluding the definition itself).
4. Focus on functions exported from internal/ packages (capitalized names in Go).

Use bash grep commands to count callers. For example, grep -r "util.FunctionName" --include="*.go" /bench/home/work | grep -v "func " | wc -l

Report the function with the highest fan-in and the approximate caller count.

content.text: Now let me extract all the exported function/method names with their package names and count their references. Let me first get the package names and function names systematically.

input.command:
for f in $(find /bench/home/work/internal -name "*.go" ! -name "*_test.go"); do
  pkg=$(grep "^package " "$f" | head -1 | awk '{print $2}')
  grep -E "^func [A-Z]|^func \(.*\) [A-Z]" "$f" | while read -r line; do
    # Extract function/method name
    if echo "$line" | grep -q "^func ("; then
      # Method: func (r *Receiver) MethodName(...)
      method=$(echo "$line" | sed 's/^func ([^)]*) \([A-Za-z0-9_]*\).*/\1/')
      echo "$pkg.$method"
    else
      # Function: func FuncName(...)
      func_name=$(echo "$line" | sed 's/^func \([A-Za-z0-9_]*\).*/\1/')
      echo "$pkg.$func_name"
    fi
  done
done | sort -u
input.description: Extract all exported function/method names with package prefix
